title: cross-team engineering leadership weekly staff notes - 2026-08-10
content:
Date: 2026-08-10
Time: 09:00-10:00 PT
Location: Zoom / #eng-serving-runtime Slack channel
Attendees: Aisha Patel (chair), Marcus Li, Sofia Hernández, Ben Carter, Ruth Kim, Devon O'Neal, Emma Ross (notes)
Absent: none

Purpose: Weekly cross-team sync for serving runtime leadership — surface updates, blockers, canary/rollout status, SRE/observability flags, and alignment on near-term priorities.

Agenda:
- Quick round-robin updates (each subteam)
- Canary rollout status for quantized v2 kernels (CAN-1023)
- Incident review: increased tail latency in us-west on 2026-08-08 (SRV-8942)
- Observability gaps and short-term dashboards to add
- Hiring and resourcing highlights for Q3
- Action items and next steps

Notes / Discussion:
1) Round-robin updates
- Serving Runtime (Marcus): Canary for quantized v2 kernels is at 18% of traffic on dedicated clusters. Early latency numbers look good for median but tail (p95/p99) shows a ~12% regression for long-sequence workloads (>2k tokens). We paused canary on us-west for two pools and rolled back those hosts while keeping global canary at reduced traffic. See CAN-1023 and PR #462.
- Observability (Sofia): Tracing instrumentation added to kernel selection path last week — we now capture kernel decision latencies and per-kernel token time. Need to add a p99 per-kernel metric to the dashboard. Also flagged gaps around multi-tenant cost attribution during fallbacks.
- Private Deployments (Ben): On-prem package for customer X is in final validation. Found an incompatibility with their older CUDA 11.8 driver that affects quantized kernels; provided a patched container image. We'll add a compatibility matrix to Confluence.
- Console & Rollouts (Ruth): Rollout UI update deployed to staging. New canary control allows per-region throttles. Need product review for edge cases (canary + fallback to smaller model family).
- SRE / Infra (Devon): Incident SRV-8942 root cause looks like a combination of kernel selection hot path + a small regression in KV cache eviction policy that caused cache churn under bursty traffic. Mitigation steps applied and full rollback for affected hosts completed. We recommend a short-term throttle rule to reduce burst load while teams tune cache policy.

2) Canary rollout details (CAN-1023)
- Current plan: step traffic 0% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over four days if no regression.
- Observed: median token latency improved by ~6% for standard sequences; p99 increased for long sequences on certain GPUs (A100-sxm vs A100-pcie differences suspected).
- Temporary measure: pin long-sequence workloads to legacy kernel until we identify root cause.
- Owners: Marcus to lead investigation with kernel team; Sofia to add per-kernel p99 dashboard tile by EOD 2026-08-11.

3) Incident SRV-8942 follow-up
- Timeline: 2026-08-08 14:10PT spike in tail latency affecting ~7% of requests in us-west. Degraded latency correlated with cache evictions.
- Impact: increase in retries and a small uptick in customer error reports (CS ticket queue). No data loss.
- Root cause (prelim): change in kv-eviction heuristic (merged last sprint) interacted poorly with new kernel memory pattern for quantized models.
- Fixes: reverted eviction heuristic for affected pools; tactical throttle rule created. Longer-term: redesign eviction policy to account for kernel memory footprints.
- Owners / timeline: Devon + Marcus to draft proposal for eviction redesign by 2026-08-17; schedule design review with SRE and Applied ML.

4) Observability and dashboards
- Action: add per-kernel p50/p95/p99 metrics, kernel-decision latency, and per-route cost attribution for fallback events.
- Slack alerting: create an alert on p99 token latency deviation >20% for 15m across any region.
- Owner: Sofia (dashboard), Ruth (alert config) — target 2026-08-12.

5) Private / Dedicated customer notes
- Customer X (on-prem) reported CUDA compatibility issue — Ben to follow up and confirm they are on patched image.
- Enterprise procurement question: clarify SLA math for dedicated reserved pools with burst capacity — send standard language to sales. Owner: Ruth.

6) Hiring / resourcing
- Two new senior infra hires expected to start in September; interviews continuing for one more SRE.
- Coverage: leadership agreed to temporary on-call rotation shift for week of 2026-08-24 while two engineers are on PTO. Devon to publish rota by 2026-08-14.

7) Open risks / blockers
- Kernel p99 regression for long sequences (blocker for completing canary at scale).
- CUDA compatibility matrix missing for some enterprise customers (blocker for Private rollout).
- Observability gaps could slow root-cause analysis for future incidents.

Action items (owner — due):
- Marcus: run detailed kernel perf comparison (A100-sxm vs A100-pcie) for long-sequence workloads and post results to CAN-1023 — due 2026-08-12.
- Sofia: add per-kernel p99 dashboard tile + set Slack alert for p99 deviation — due 2026-08-11.
- Devon: complete eviction-policy proposal draft and coordinate design review — due 2026-08-17.
- Ben: confirm patched container image validated with Customer X and update compatibility matrix on Confluence — due 2026-08-13.
- Ruth: circulate standard SLA language for Dedicated pools to Sales and legal — due 2026-08-14.
- Emma Ross (notes): consolidate CS ticket list related to SRV-8942 and provide a short summary to customer success — due 2026-08-11.

Decisions made:
- Pause canary increase to 20% until kernel p99 issue understood.
- Short-term rollback of kv-eviction heuristic in affected pools.
- Add per-kernel observability as high priority before next canary step.

Misc / notes to self:
- Follow up with Applied ML on model memory pattern differences that might change kernel selection behavior.
- Remind product to add explicit fallback cost visibility in the Console (helpful for enterprise SLAs).

Next meeting: 2026-08-17 09:00 PT
